shadow:
There is a particular grey that has nothing to do with sadness. Sadness at least has a pull to it, a direction. This has none. It is the flat middle of a day where nothing pushes and nothing draws, the hour when the kettle, the inbox, the same drive to the same place all arrive with the colour drained out. A dog can lie on a step for an afternoon and want for nothing. A person in this grey wants out of it, and that wanting is the whole trouble.

The mind reads the flatness as a verdict, decides the days themselves are at fault, and starts hunting for a charge, any charge, to prove otherwise.

Most people treat the grey as a thing to escape. That is the misread. The flatness is not the bottom of anything. It sits in the slack centre where no charge runs, and a charge can be picked up there as easily as it was lost. Sink all the way into the dullness instead of clawing at its edges, and somewhere down in it the air begins to move again.
repressive: Some meet the grey by going quiet inside it. They stop reaching, decide the flatness is just the shape of their life now, and let it settle. It reads as a kind of peace. Underneath, something has simply been put down.
reactive: Others meet it by bolting. New city, new scene, new appetite, anything with an edge, never resting long enough to feel the flatness catch up. It looks like a life full of motion. None of the moving has a direction it trusts.
gift:
Something shifts when a person stops treating the flat hour as an enemy. They stay in it, stop hunting the charge, and the grey they were braced against turns out to be a vessel that looked empty and was full the whole time. This is Magnetism, and it is slower than most people expect a gift to be.

It runs at the pace of the earth, not the pace of a phone. There is a frequency the planet itself holds, a low and steady pulse, and a body that comes near it stops fighting the rhythm of its own days. The agitated mind hears that slowness and calls it dullness. It is the opposite. It is the speed at which a forest grows back over a road.

Magnetism draws things toward a life without effort, people and chance and what is needed, because the life has stopped pushing and started holding. The dishes, the commute, the unremarkable Tuesday become the field where everything happens, not the dull part to get through before the real thing starts. The grey of the Shadow was never absence. It was the colour of the Gift before anyone leaned close enough to feel it.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the holding becomes a flowering, and not one bloom but a whole tree going off at once, in every direction, faster than a mind could ever track or arrange. This is Florescence. It cannot be hurried or earned. It arrives the way spring arrives, on its own clock, to no schedule a person sets.

What marks someone here is how plainly ordinary they have become. The one who reached the mountain has walked back down it and is doing the dishes, telling a joke, getting things a little wrong on purpose so as not to be set above anyone. Holiness that floats free of the earth has been quietly refused. The love here works by staying close, by staying human, even letting itself look weak if that is what keeps it near.

Look back from this and the long grey stretch reads differently. The flatness that felt like a life with the colour gone was the slack centre where the charge first gathered. It was the still ground. It is where the whole tree came up from.
